source: Somsak Wannasaree, "Banana Orchards" (Khmer translation, 1997), section 9 (fertilizing and watering)
text:
This source gives general nutrient-balance guidance for banana that complements the month-by-month fertilizer schedule found in the newer MAFF manual. Because banana fruiting is especially demanding on potassium, the recommended nitrogen:phosphorus:potassium ratio for banana is approximately 1:1:3 — in other words, roughly three times as much potassium as nitrogen or phosphorus, reflecting potassium's outsized role in fruit filling, sweetness, and overall bunch quality.

Application should be little-and-often rather than one or two large doses: the source suggests amounts on the order of 60g per clump per application, applied repeatedly through the growing season rather than as a single heavy application, since a plant that gets a steady, moderate nutrient supply grows more evenly than one that is over-fed once and then neglected.

Organic matter (compost, manure, or decomposing leaf litter left in place) is recommended alongside chemical fertilizer, both to improve soil structure and moisture retention and to supply trace minerals that a chemical NPK blend alone may not provide. Some farmers also interplant a nitrogen-fixing cover crop between banana rows to supplement soil nitrogen naturally over time.
